full_judgment:
2. The case of the plaintiff-respondent is that the land of schedule 'A' together with other land of RS khatian No. 246 of Mouza Lalkhan Bazar formerly PS Kotwali, at present PS Double Mooring, District Chittagong originally belonged to Sailendra Krishna, Pram Krishna and Gokhul Krishna, sons of late Bajendra Kumar Roy in 131/2 annas share and Harendra Kumar, son of Ajit Chandra Roy in 21 annas share; that accordingly RS khatian was prepared and finally published in the name of aforesaid owners; that by amicable arrangement; Harendra Kumar surrendered his share in the land of said khatian in favour of Sailendra Krishna, Pran Krishna and Gokhul Krishan and they were in possession of the same on payment of rent to the superior owners and that subsequently the aforesaid owners transferred their interest in the suit khatian to their wives Mrs Lalita Roy, Purnarama Roy and Rajubala Roy respectively. 

 3. It is stated that major portion of the said khatian was hilly jungle land and a part of it including schedule-A was ballad; that aforesaid original owners used to possess the same by giving lease to tenants; that accordingly, out of schedule 'A' land, the aforesaid original owners leased out 0.140 sahasrangsha i.e. 7 gandas of land, as described in schedule 'B' to defendant No. 31, Khaled Solaiman, on 19-7-1938 by acceptance of salami and rent and that the defendant No. 31 Khaled Solaiman used to possess the lease-hold land by cultivating it through abraders on payment of rent to the landlords and their transferees who recognized and admitted defendant No. 31, Khaled Solaiman as raiyat under them. It is further stated that subsequently, with the expansion of Chittagong town, habitation and construction of dwelling houses started in the surrounding land; that accordingly, the defendant No. 31, Khaled Solaiman, also constructed 2 kutcha dwelling houses in part of the schedule 'B' land which appertained to Municipal holding No. 150 and was possessing the same on payment of rents and taxes and thus the defendant No. 31, Khaled Solaiman, was in possession of the schedule 'B' land as tenant and by exercising his own right openly and adversely to other defendants for over statutory period of limitation; that while the defendant No. 31, Khaled Solaiman, was in khas possession of the entire schedule 'B' land, he sold 4 gandas equivalent to 0.80 sataks as described in schedule 'B'(1) together with the house appertaining to Municipal holding No. 150 to the plaintiff by a registered kabala dated 27th May, 1977 for valuable consideration and put the plaintiff in possession of the same. 

 4. The further case of the plaintiff is that after purchase, the plaintiff constructed one more kootchar house on schedule B(1) land and repaired the previous houses and let out to six temporary tenants and that the plaintiff has also undertaken construction of a 4-storied building on. part of schedule B(1) land and has completed construction of ground floor, safety tank and pucca boundary wall as per plan of CDA approved vide BC case No. 467 of 1977 and installed WASA water lines and electric lines and that on the basis of plaintiff's purchase deed and possession the name of the plaintiff has been recorded, in draft BS khatian. 

 5. It is further stated that Saleh Ahmed, predecessor of defendants Nos. 1 to 9 and 10 to 15, filed Title Suit No. 29 of 1959 in the court of the Subordinate Judge, First Court, Chittagong for declaration of tenancy khas dakhali right in 4 kanis of land out of which 19½ gandas in schedule 'A' and balance in RS plot Nos. 60 and 67 of khatian No. 246 on the allegation that the aforesaid owners granted 9 years' lease of 4 Kanis of land of RS plot Nos. 60, 66, 67 to one Pitambar; that Pitamber died leaving son Mukhia Jamadar and he was in possession of the same and while in possession he sold 4 kanis of land to Abdus Sobhan Chowdhury, predecessor or defendants Nos. 1 to 15 and put him in possession of the land except the land covered by a house in which the seller was in permissive possession for some time and that subsequently, Mukhia did not give possession of house and also denied their title and hence they filed the said suit. 

 11. It is further stated that Mukhia Jamader while in possession of some portion of the purchased land of Abdus Sobhan Chowdhury, on permission, created certain fraudulent documents in the name of his wife, Bishuni and illegally inducted some persons in the said land; that the legal heirs of Abdus Sobhan Chowdhury, Saleh Ahmed, predecessor of defendant Nos. 1 to 9 and defendant Nos. 10 to 15, brought Title Suit No. 29 of 1959 in the court of Additional Subordinate Judge, Chittagong against Mukhia and other persons who were illegally in the land in collusion with Mukhia, for establishment of title and confirmation of possession and obtained decree on 10-9-1964 except some portion of RS plot No. 60; that these defendants are the owners of 19 gandas 2 Karas land of RS plot No. 66 from its eastern side within definite and specified boundary having no connection whatsoever with the rest of the land of RS plot No. 66; that this specific land was the land obtained by Mukhia Jamader by settlement from the land-lord; that Mukhia himself possessed this 19 gandas 2 karas specifically in his tenancy right with his other lands forming a separate tenancy under the landlord and by transfer from him, defendants predecessors Abdus Sobhan Chowdhury possessed the same and after his death, his legal heirs i.e. the defendants, possessed it separately and specifically forming a separate holding under separate jam having no connection with other portion of the RS plot No. 66; and that defendant's decretal land have been recorded In the PS Khatian in the name of their predecessor themselves. It is further stated that these defendants are in joint possession of their 19 gandas 2 karas land with the rest of the land of said RS plot and their holding is separate and they have no co-sharers for their land and no question of partition of their 19 ganders 2 karas land arises with the rest of land of RS plot No. 66 by metes and bounds; that the plaintiff nor his alleged vendor defendant No. 31, Khaled Solaiman, has or had any right, title and legal possession in the suit land of schedule 'B' or 'B(1)' and that the plaintiff and the alleged vendors are very recent trespassers in the suit land who collusively created some documents and papers for the purpose of this suit and that the plaintiffs have no title and possession in the suit land and thus the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 18. Mr Omar Faruque, the learned Advocate for the respondents, submits that the land in schedule A together with other land of RS khatian No. 246 of mouza Lalkhan Bazar formerly PS Kotwali, at present PS Double Mooring, District Chittagong originally belonged to Sailendra Krishna, Pram Krishna and Gokul Krishna in 13½ annas share and Harendra Kumar in 2½ annas share; that accordingly, RS khatian was prepared and finally published in the name of aforesaid owners; that by amicable arrangement, Harendra Kumar surrendered his share in the land of said khatian in favour of Sailendra Krishna, Pram Krishna and Gokul Krishna and they were in possession of the same on payment of rent to the superior landlord and that the subsequently aforesaid owner transferred their interest in the suit khatian to their wives Mrs Lalita Roy, Purnarama Roy and Rajubala Roy respectively. He further submits their the original owners used to possess the same by giving lease to tenants; that accordingly out of schedule 'A' land, the aforesaid original owners leased out 0.140 sahasrangsha i.e. 7 gandas of land as described in schedule 'B' to defendant No. 31 Khaled Solaiman, that while the defendant No. 31, Khaled Solaiman, was in khas possession of the entire schedule 'B' land, he sold 4 gandas equivalent to 0.80 sataks as described in schedule B(1) together with the house appertaining to Municipal holding No. 150 to the plaintiff by a registered kabala dated 27th May, 1977 for valuable consideration and put the plaintiff in possession of the same. It is further submitted that after purchase the plaintiff constructed one more kutcha house on schedule B(1) land and repaired the previous houses and let out to 6 temporary tenants. The plaintiff Moulana Mohammad Harun-ur-Rashid has also undertaken construction of 4-storied building on part of schedule B(1) land and has completed construction of ground floor, safety tank and pucca boundary wall as per plan of CDA approved plan vide BC Case No. 467 of 1977 and installed WASA water lines and electric lines. It is further submitted that the defendants title in 19½ gandas in suit plot has been declared but in the aforesaid plot the total area of land is 41½ kanis which is much in excess of the land of the share of defendant Nos. 1 to 15; that the original, landlords before leasing out the land of Patambar, out of the suit plot No. 66 leased out 7½ gandas land to plaintiff's predecessor the defendant No. 31, Khaled Solaiman, as such there is no clash of title between the plaintiff and defendants No. 1 to 15 and other co-sharers and the same is required to be partitioned. Mr Faruque further submits that the impugned judgment and decree was legally passed which should not be interfered.
